replies.body: This is intentional. `apache-httpclient-4.3:library` has no `gradle.properties` with `otel.stable=true`, so it's an alpha artifact and its deprecations follow the alpha policy: "may be removed in the next minor release". The 3.0 removal contract you're referring to applies to `instrumentation-api`, which is a stable artifact — that's why `HttpClientAttributesExtractorBuilder` is worded differently. Same reasoning for line 107.

threads.body:
[General] This also enables enumeration for the deprecated request-header setter. That setter still delegates to a builder that converts its names into an `IncludeExclude`, so an existing literal `"*"` is now evaluated as a wildcard and captures every request header (potentially including credentials), contrary to the documented compatibility guarantee. Add a distinct literal-name path for the deprecated setter and a `"*"` regression test.

This issue also appears on line 55 of the same file.

replies.body:
This was real, and it's fixed — though the premise is now out of date on both ends. `setCapturedRequestHeaders` no longer builds an `IncludeExclude`; it delegates to the underlying builder's exact-name setter, which routes through `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact` and matches by `Set#contains` on lowercased names, never through `IncludeExclude#matches`. So a literal `"*"` looks for a header named `*` and captures nothing, as before. The javadoc now says the names are matched literally and points at the replacement as the one that matches patterns.

On the regression test: the `"*"` case is covered in `HttpHeadersTest` (`deprecatedCapturedHeadersSettersMatchHeaderNamesLiterally`) on the base branch, which is where the literal matching is actually implemented. The module-level code is a single delegating call with no matching logic of its own, and these modules expose no seam to build the instrumenter without a full HTTP round trip, so a duplicate here would cost a lot and pin nothing extra.
